accuracy.evidence: Definitions follow the national curriculum glossary and Key Stage 2 programme of study: register as the formality chosen for the reader and situation, cohesion as linking between sentences through connectives and other devices, form as the type of text, purpose as inform, persuade or entertain. Tone is kept separate from register (sarcastic can be formal or informal). The hedgehog facts were checked against the State of Britain's Hedgehogs 2018 report (rural road-casualty counts fell by between a third and a half from 2002 to 2017, so the lab says 'fell by up to half' rather than 'halved') and Hedgehog Street advice on fence gaps; hedgehogs are nocturnal and eat slugs and beetles. Every connective answer was checked: for example (example), however (contrast), because (cause), then (time order, spare).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real slips at this age: thinking the facts matter but the register does not (predict option 'Either', challenge 'nomatter'); thinking formal is always better (sending the stiff version to a best friend says it sounds cold); confusing tone with register and form (challenge 'term', 'tone', 'form' items, m1, m4); using any linking word, especially then, regardless of the relationship (the spare Then tile and the feedback naming the needed job; m5, p2); mistaking an opinion or a question for evidence (challenge 'evid', m3, m9); and reading sarcasm literally (challenge 'tone', p4).

lab_distinct.evidence: No other flagship lab has a register dial that rewrites a real message at three levels of formality and judges it against a named reader, or a paragraph whose gaps each need a different cohesive relation. The purpose sort, connective fill and technique labelling all act on writing choices only, so the lab could not be relabelled for another topic. The 30% shingle gate passed against every other flagship lab, including flagpat, flagprint and flaghelp.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner feels each term before the text names it: the same request turns from 'Hey! … Gonna hand it in Fri' to 'Dear Mr Ali … Please may I' as the dial moves, so register is seen as a choice for a reader; the friend message sent formally is rejected as cold, so formal is not always right. Gap feedback names the relation each tile shows against the one needed, and the technique labels each state what the device does to the reader. The free step adds two new readers to test the idea.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Either: the facts are the same' for the head teacher email (the lab refuses to send the informal version), 'To inform: it tells you about the fair' for a persuasive line (the sort rejects it with the reason), and 'Long, fancy words' for cohesion (the paragraph links only when the right connectives go in, with no long words at all). The win message names the prediction and why the right answer holds.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating kinds (register for an editor, name the term, read the tone, choose a connective, spot perspective, pick evidence, name the form) with answer order rotated. Each of fourteen wrong options has its own message naming the slip, for example 'Tone is the feeling … how formal it is, is the register', 'Because gives a reason … here it is a contrast', 'Third person uses he, she or they. I means first person', and '"The worst place ever" is an opinion'.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and concrete examples (Hey! versus Dear Mr Ali; however, because, for example) and passed the kid FK limit in validate_lessons despite the technical terms, each defined in plain words the first time it appears. Lab prompts define the term in one sentence before the task. Adult text passed its limit and separates register, tone, form, cohesion and coherence clearly.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph introduces one or two terms with an example and nothing else. The adult text has one job per paragraph: curriculum expectation, definitions, named mistakes, and a home activity. Each lab step adds a new group of terms (register, purpose and form, cohesion, techniques); there are no decorative steps.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 375 px with touch: the register message wraps inside its bubble, the dial labels sit at the ends of a full-width track and the knob can be dragged with a finger; purpose bins show a tick and first word for each sorted card so nothing spills; the cohesion gaps wrap the rest of each sentence beside the slot without clipping; technique chips are two columns of large targets. Every canvas action has a full-size button below. The iPhone 13 walkthrough passed.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin (less and more formal, send, new reader, each purpose, each connective, clear, each technique). The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the reader, dial level and full message, the current opening, the whole paragraph with gaps, or the current phrase. Feedback and challenge results land in polite live regions; axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) reported no violations in either theme on desktop and phone.
